This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 28.02.2023 at about 7.05 p.m. he had been riding his Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05- JZ-7500 near NPS School Junction, Paduka Mandira Road, P.P.Layout, Uttarahalli, Bengaluru, at that time, another Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05- LM-727 came from opposite direction in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against his vehicle, due to the said impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to pathway Hospital, thereafter shifted to Rajshekar Hospital and he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
transportation, medicines and nourishment.
3. At the time of the accident, he was aged about 47 years, hale and healthy, working as an employee at SCCH-5 Medical Store at Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
due to this accident he is unable to continue his work and undergone severe mental stress and agony.

Out of this accident crime No.81/2023 is registered against the rider of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-LM-0727 before the Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the said offending scooter, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and d e n i e d a v e r m e n t s o f t h e p e t i t i o n . F u r t h e r d e n i e d i s s u a n c e o f p o l i c y b e a r i n g No.140522223760048912 in favour of SCCH-5 respondent No.2 in respect of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LM-727.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JZ-7500 were not made as parties.
Further denied occurrence of the accident and involvement of alleged offending vehicle in the accident.

Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.

5. Respondent No.2/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further submitted that, he is R.C.Owner of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-LM-0727 and it is insured with respondent No.1 vide policy SCCH-5 No.1405222237600048912 which was valid from 14.07.2022 to 13.07.2023.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.02.2023 at about 7.05 p.m. near NPS School Junction, Paduka Mandira Road, P.P.Layout, Uttaharahalli, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent riding of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LM-727 and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
SCCH-5 7.
In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand, Legal Manager of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed evidence.
8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
: : REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated SCCH-5 in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

3 regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet along with statement of witnesses is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.13.
10.

sentences.text:
On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, charge sheet with statement of witnesses, sketch, IMV Report and spot mahazar corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 28.02.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.
Per contra, the Legal Manager of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and exhibited authorization SCCH-5 letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 28.02.2023 at about 7.05 p.m. when he was riding a Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA- 05-JZ-7500 near NPS School Junction, Paduka Mandira Road, P.P.Layout, Uttaharahalli, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments addressed by the petitioner's counsel are support to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of the rider of the offending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LM-0727.

Under such circumstances,
considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal SCCH-5 comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 47 years, to prove his age,
petitioner has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.15, wherein birth year is mentioned as 1975, the alleged accident was occurred in the year 2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.15, age of the petitioner is considered as 48 years as on the date of the accident.
Further petitioner was working as an employee at a Medical Store at Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

In this regard,
petitioner has not produced any income proof documents.
14. As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained abrasion over left forearm, laceration over right SCCH-5 arm, soft tissue injury over right and left shoulder, which are simple in nature.

To prove the same, petitioner has exhibited copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6 issued by Pathway Hospital, case sheet marked as Ex.P.7, certificate issued from Rajshekar Hospital marked as Ex.P.8, diagnosis report marked as Ex.P.9, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.10, Pathway Hospital Medical bills of Rs.7,537/- marked as Ex.P.11, OPD Bill of Rajashekar Hospital of Rs.21,006/-
marked as Ex.P.12, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.14.

On perusal of the said medical bills it is noticed that, petitioner has exhibited medical bills which are not considered for total medical bills i.e., in Ex.P.11 for Rs.13,160/- and Ex.P.12 amounts to Rs.72,657/- though they have taken into consideration, because they are SCCH-5 available in the file.
Hence petitioner is entitled for the said all medical bills amounting to Rs.85,817/-.
15. Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated him nor produced the disability certificate towards the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

16. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.1,35,817/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

17. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing SCCH-5 No.140522223760048912 which is valid for the period from 14.07.2022 to 13.07.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 28.02.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.2 shall go against respondent No.1, so that, respondent No.1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:
For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.1,35,817/-
(Rupees One Lakh Thirty Five SCCH-5 Thousand Eight Hundred Seventeen Only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
